notes: §1985:VI.6.12.3 SR3: 'The sentence ENTER COBOL must follow the last other-language statement in order to indicate to the compiler where a return to COBOL source language takes place.' The compiler has no other-language mode: StatementBinder#BindEnter binds ENTER <language> as a BoundNop at 85 (VersionConformancePass#VisitEnterStatement gates it only from 2002) and the text after it is read as COBOL, so an in-line ENTER FORTRAN. with no closing ENTER COBOL compiles and the 'other-language' text runs as COBOL; under WiseOwl's choice not to provide ENTER (§1985:I.1.5.2.5.5) it must be refused. Probes at 85: e5 (ENTER FORTRAN. DISPLAY "INLINE-OTHER". STOP RUN.) prints BEFORE INLINE-OTHER rc=0; e2 (FORTRAN text then ENTER COBOL.) refused only by COBOL0001 on the FORTRAN syntax; ENTER COBOL followed by a statement in its sentence refused COBOL6973 (StatementPosition#EnterEndsSentence); at 2002 COBOL0902. The witness (ENTER FORTRAN SUBRTN. ENTER COBOL. skipped by GO TO) passes but speaks of no other-language statement. kb/Work PB5308 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-03.json).

next.reason: 1985: "The sentence ENTER COBOL must follow the last other-language statement"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the ENTER statement; no candidate covers other-language entry or ENTER COBOL". No 2023 clause covers the ENTER statement, and no worded candidate addresses returning to COBOL from other-language statements. The feature is absent from 2023.
